transcript.text: Beko vented dryer, drum goes round fine but it's just blowing cold air. Had it about 6 years. What part do I need?

The usual failed part on a vented dryer that still tumbles but blows genuinely cold is the heater element, often together with (or stopped by) its thermal cut-out/thermostat. With it switched off and unplugged, clean the door fluff filter and check the hose all the way to the outside vent for fluff, crushing or kinks. Then use a normal high-heat programme for 10–15 minutes; if it remains completely cold with a clear vent, the heater/thermal protection circuit is the leading suspect and will need testing/replacement by a competent repairer.
[Helpful to see: image "Tumble dryer runs but doesn't heat — what to check" — If the drum turns but the clothes stay wet, it's usually a heating fault — and the most common cause is restricted airflow, which you can fix yourself. Clean the fluff filter and the condenser and clear the vents/ducts. Switch the dryer off and let it cool first.]

Did all that. Filter was pretty full and the hose had a sag packed with fluff, both cleaned out and airflow at the hose end is decent now. Still stone cold after 20 mins on high. The hose was properly clogged before this happened. It's a Beko DV7110, so what's the part number for the element or thermostat?

With the previous severe vent blockage now cleared but the dryer still completely cold, the fault is very likely in the heater circuit — most likely the thermal cut-out/thermostat opened due to overheating, or the heater element itself has gone open-circuit. A competent repairer should isolate and unplug the dryer, then continuity-test the heater and its thermal protection devices; that identifies which component has actually failed and avoids fitting the wrong part. If the thermal cut-out has failed, the underlying airflow route also needs checking for internal fluff build-up before it is put back into use.

candidates: Heater element or its thermal cut-out/thermostat failure (high)
Restricted venting or fluff blockage causing the overheat protection to operate (medium)
